Design decision from Jack Heart (2026-11-22) on Fork #6 (web UI capabilities):

"6b" — Interactive control plane (cancel runs / terminate machines from the Status & Machines pages, with proper auth/CSRF/safety).

Consolidated design direction from Jack Heart across all 6 architectural forks:
1. Data & speed: "You own your own data" (files stay the durable user-owned record), AND a derived/indexed DB copy for speed is explicitly desired. Sub-second graph loads is a complete requirement; use the fastest, most reliable data flow.
2. Server topology: Process split vs single process on the host is an implementation detail (keep it clean/safe).
3. Page topology: Keep static `etude report` conceptually the same (printable, git-committable artifact). Served experiment page combines two async-loading components on ONE webpage (operational status + `report()`), alongside `/`, `/machines`, and per-run live view (`/runs/...`) with table-stakes live curves, console logs, config, checkpoints.
4. Canonical `report()`: Code, not config; pulled and executed in isolation from the experiment's declared git hash.
5. Live links / local lifecycle: Live links apply when a live server (local, team, or eventually hosted) is configured/running; no background daemon required without a live server.
6. Capabilities: Interactive control plane (cancel runs / terminate machines from the UI, with appropriate auth/CSRF/audit).
